{"self_assessment": "Impact: I laid most of the bottom line of the fish (stroke 2), about 47 dominoes over roughly two and a half minutes. That line forms the lower half of the body and, with the top line, gives the fish its recognizable outline. Early on I fetched a full load of 40 dominoes for the shared bin, so builders had supply when they started. My inspections of the nose area, where the two lines join, showed the whole run connected, and the start domino traced through all 101 standing dominoes by eye.

Execution: I took the bottom stroke when it was assigned and queued it so it started as soon as the top line reached the nose. I laid it steadily in batches without stalling. I inspected the nose joint twice and the full run once the build was done. I then told the table to keep hands off so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed with short status updates on where the bottom line stood and what I was checking. I made clear which stroke was mine, so Omar and I didn't double up on the same work. I also left the tail tip to Omar so we weren't working on top of each other. I kept my hands clear of other people's areas to reduce the chance of bumps.

Leadership: Once my stroke was done, I moved to verification instead of looking for more to build. I checked the full connectivity and set the final hands-off rule for the last minutes. I made sure the table's attention stayed on keeping the finished fish intact, which gave us a clean push.", "my_share_percent": 30}
